text:
(1) This Act may be called the Legal Metrology 
Act, 2009.

section_title: Short title, extent and commencement
text: (2) It extends to the whole of India.

section_title: Provisions of this Act to override provisions of any other law

Act or in any instrument having effect by virtue of any enactment other than this Act. 
CHAPTER II 
STANDARD WEIGHTS AND MEASURES

section_title: Units of weights and measures to be based on metric system
text:
Every unit of weight or measure 
shall be in accordance with the metric system based on the international system of units.

section_title: Base unit of weights and measures
text: (1) The base unit of—

section_title: Base unit of weights and measures
text: (i) length shall be the metre;

section_title: Base unit of weights and measures
text: (ii) mass shall be the kilogram;

section_title: Base unit of weights and measures
text: (iii) time shall be the second;

section_title: Base unit of weights and measures
text: (iv) electric current shall be the ampere;

section_title: Base unit of weights and measures
text: (v) thermodynamic temperature shall be the kelvin;

section_title: Base unit of weights and measures
text: (vi) luminous intensity shall be the candela; and

section_title: Base unit of weights and measures
text: (vii) amount of substance shall be the mole.

section_title: Base unit of weights and measures
text:
(2) The specifications of the base units mentioned in sub -section (1), derived units and other units 
shall be such as may be prescribed.

section_title: Base unit of numeration
text:
(1) The base unit of numeration shall be the unit of the international 
form of Indian numerals.

section_title: Base unit of numeration
text: (2) Every numeration shall be made in accordance with the decimal system.

section_title: Base unit of numeration
text:
(3) The decimal multiples and sub -multiples of the numerals shall be of such denominations and be 
written in such manner as may be prescribed.

section_title: Standard units of weights and measures
text:
(1) The base units of weights and measures specified 
in section 5 shall be the standard units of weights and measures.

section_title: Standard units of weights and measures
text:
(2) The base unit of numeration specified in section 6 shall be the standard unit of numeration.

section_title: Standard weight, measures or numeral
text:
(1) Any weight or measure which conforms to the 
standard unit of such weight or measure and also conforms to such of the provisions of section 7 as are 
applicable to it shall be the standard weight or measure.

section_title: Standard weight, measures or numeral
text: (2) Any numeral which conforms to the provisions of section 6 shall be the standard numeral.

section_title: Standard weight, measures or numeral
text:
(3) No weight, measure or numeral, other than the standard weight, measure or numeral, shall be used 
as a standard weight, measure or numeral.

section_title: Standard weight, measures or numeral
text:

weight or measure specified under section 8:

section_title: Reference, secondary and working standard
text:
(1) The reference standards, secondary standards 
and working standards of weights and measures shall be such as may be prescribed.

section_title: Reference, secondary and working standard

in such manner and after payment of such fee as may be prescribed.

section_title: Reference, secondary and working standard
text:
(3) Every reference standard, secondary standard and working standard which is not verified and 
stamped in accordance with the provisions of sub-section (2) shall not be deemed to be a valid standard.

section_title: Any custom, usage, etc., contrary to standard weight, measure or numeration to be void
text:
Any custom, usage, practice or method of whatever nature which permits a person to demand, receive or 
cause to be demanded or received, any quantity of article, thing or service in excess of or less than, the 
quantity specified by weight, measure or number in the contract or other agreement in relation to the said 
article, thing or service, shall be void. 
CHAPTER III

text:
(1) The Central 
Government may, by notification, appoint a Director of legal metrology, Additional Director, Joint 
Director, Deputy Director, Assistant Director and other employees for exercising the powers and 
discharging the duties conferred or imposed on them by or under this Act in relation to inter -State trade 
and commerce.

section_title: Forfeiture
text:
(1) Every non-standard or unverified weight or measure, and every package made in 
contravention of section 18, used in the course of, or in relation to, any trade and commerce and seized 
under section 15, shall be liable to be forfeited to the State Government: 
 Provided that such unverified weight or measure shall not be forfeited to the State Government if the 
person from whom such weight or measure was seized gets the same verified and stamped within such 
time as may be prescribed.

section_title: Forfeiture

(2) Every weight, measure or other goods seized under section 15 but not forfeited under 
sub-section (1), shall be disposed of by such authority and in such manner as may be prescribed.

text:

section_title: Non-standard weights and measures not to be imported
text:
No weight or measure, whether

weight or measure established by or under this Act.

text:

section_title: Verification and stamping of weight or measure
text:
(1) Every person having any weight or

being, or is intended or is likely to be, used by him in any transaction or for protection, shall, before 
putting such weight or measure into such use, have such weight or measure verified at such place and 
during such hours as the Controller may, by general or special order, specify in this behalf, on payment of 
such fees as may be prescribed.

section_title: Verification and stamping of weight or measure

verification is to be done through the Government approved Test Centre.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS 
In India, uniform standards of weights and measures based on the metric system, were established in 
the year 1956, which were revised in the year 1976 with a view to give effect to the international system 
of units. Apart from it, the Standards of Weights and Measures Act, 1976 provides for establishing 
Standards of Weights and Measures, regulation of inter-State trade or commerce in weights and measures 
and other goods which are sold by weight, measure or number. In the year 1985, the Standards of Weights 
and Measures (Enforcement) Act, 1985 was enacted for enforcement of standards of weights and 
measures established by or under the 1976 Act. 
2. The advancement of technology has necessitated the review of above mentioned enactments to 
make them simple, eliminate obsolete regulations, ensure accountability and bring transparency. 
3. It has become imperative to combine the provisions of the existing two Acts to get rid of anomalies 
and make the provisions simple. It has also become necessary to keep the regulation pragmatic to the 
extent required for protecting the interest of consumers and at the same time keep the industry free from 
undue interference. It has also become necessary to recognise certain “Government approved Test 
Centres” which will be empowered to verify prescribed weight or measure.
